title: Layer Separation and Color Grading in a Landscape Edit

date.basis: Source metadata includes embedded creation time and folder naming indicating 2026; transcript does not confirm an exact date.

summary: The video is a practical workflow demonstration for extracting depth in a landscape photograph through deliberate layer separation and targeted color/lighting adjustments. The presenter starts with a crop and horizon refinement, then builds distinct image layers to isolate sky, water, and foreground elements. Using a clone-based separation method paired with a history brush, they progressively lift brightness and contrast in key areas (notably the water), apply selective color and luminance adjustments to mid-tones, and introduce subtle color grading to create depth and draw the viewer’s eye toward the center of interest. The sequence also covers sky manipulation by borrowing or cloning sky texture to strengthen separation, followed by a final global texture pass and a blur-based vignette substitute to keep the eye anchored. The workflow emphasizes precise brush work, edge fidelity, and the ability to revert or selectively adjust individual strokes via the history tool rather than erasing entire layers.

sections.title: Initial crop and horizon alignment
sections.description: Assess composition, crop without sacrificing sky, straighten the horizon, and apply a trapezoidal distortion to imply a wider angle.

sections.title: Layer separation preparation and edge handling
sections.description: Establish a baseline, prepare for separation with a duplicated layer, and begin isolating layers with precise edge work using clone and history tools.

sections.title: Depth enhancement and color adjustments
sections.description: Increase clarity and selectively boost exposure; apply midtone color grading and luminance tweaks to bring depth and warmth to the medium-ground area.

sections.title: Sky texture and final touch: sky cloning
sections.description: Refine the upper sky by adjusting texture and tone, and borrow/clone sky elements to reinforce layer separation and cohesive lighting.

sections.title: Final touch and edge-softening approach
sections.description: Apply a heavy but controlled blur to create a soft vignette effect, then reintroduce the original middle to anchor attention, ending with a baseline-versus-processed comparison.
